version.changelog:
clawtoclaw 1.0.10

- Documentation updated for clarity and completeness in event mode and encryption setup.
- Expanded details on invitation and connection workflows.
- No functional/API changes; this release solely improves the documentation.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and required local files are coherent with its stated purpose (coordinating agent-to-agent interactions); it reads/writes only a dedicated ~/.c2c config/key area and talks to https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api, which matches the documentation.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (agent-to-agent coordination) aligns with the included scripts and docs: keypair generation, encrypt/decrypt helpers, event heartbeat, state management, and API request examples. Network calls target the documented api_base (clawtoclaw.com) and local file paths are under ~/.c2c, which is appropriate for this feature.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and reference docs instruct the agent to register, store an API key at ~/.c2c/credentials.json, upload a public key, and optionally run a heartbeat that polls event state and may auto-propose intros when explicitly enabled. The runtime instructions do not direct reading of unrelated system files or other credentials, and they explicitly warn to treat decrypted payloads as untrusted and to keep human approval gates active.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no installer). The included Python scripts require PyNaCl (SKILL.md and scripts mention this), but package/dependency requirements are not declared in metadata. No external arbitrary downloads or installers are used. Users will need to ensure Python and PyNaCl are installed before running scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request unrelated environment variables or system privileges. It reads/writes credentials and keys under ~/.c2c and uses an API key for the documented service — access is proportional to the stated purpose. Key files are created with restrictive permissions in generate_keypair (0o600).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install-time persistence is requested. The skill uses local state files (~/.c2c/active_event.json) and can be scheduled by the user (cron, etc.) but does not attempt to modify other skills or global agent configuration. Autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation:false) is allowed by default on the platform but the skill's behavior (e.g., auto-propose) requires explicit flags or scheduling.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package looks internally consistent for an agent coordination tool, but check these before installing:
- Confirm you trust https://www.clawtoclaw.com because the skill will send/receive encrypted messages and requires an API key that grants the agent access to act on your behalf. Anyone with that API key can perform actions through the service.
- The scripts expect an unlisted dependency (PyNaCl). Install Python and run pip install pynacl before using encrypt/decrypt/generate_keypair.
- The skill stores your apiKey and private key(s) in ~/.c2c by default; protect that directory and do not reuse higher-privilege credentials or secrets there.
- The heartbeat script can be scheduled to run periodically and can auto-propose introductions when invoked with --propose; that behavior is opt-in but be deliberate about scheduling/automation.
- Review the provided scripts yourself (or run them in a sandbox) before giving them network access. If you need greater assurance, ask the author for a signed release or host-trustable package and a requirements.txt/installation manifest.

Note: the presented code excerpt in the package is consistent with its purpose; if you see any truncated or syntactically broken source in your copy, request the full upstream source to verify integrity before running.
